target_customer: Restaurants, cloud kitchens, caterers and food processors in Bengaluru that buy fruit and vegetables
problem: Roughly 30 percent of a farmer's harvest goes unsold because of cosmetic appearance, while commercial kitchens pay full price for produce they often cut or puree anyway.
business_model: B2B produce distribution: buys cosmetically imperfect produce directly from farms and resells to kitchens at a discount of 25 to 30 percent, margin on the spread

founders.name: Arpit Agarwal
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and in Inc42 (2024-02-27). Neither gives a background.

founders.name: Sakshi Agarwal
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and in Inc42 (2024-02-27). Neither gives a background.

competitors.name: Ninjacart
competitors.what: Farm to retailer and restaurant fresh produce supply chain in Bengaluru, not specialised in imperfect produce
competitors.traction_then: 2016 coverage reports about Rs 4 crore revenue per month
competitors.funding_then: Not stated in the cited snippet

technical_complexity.rationale: Logistics, sorting and sourcing operations rather than novel technology; the hard parts are cold chain, fleet and farm aggregation.

defensibility.rationale: Direct farm sourcing and own delivery fleet help, but Ninjacart and other produce suppliers could add an ugly produce line. Inc42 reports 3,000 partner farmers and 1,500 kitchens by 2024, which is a modest base.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows a larger player copying the ugly produce wedge for kitchens in India. The company stayed small and raised only a seed in 2024.

market_need_then: The company says about 30 percent of harvest goes unsold for looks and that its produce costs kitchens 25 to 30 percent less. These are company statements from its website.

identity.logo: Wordmark with the tagline saving what's good (from logo alt text)
identity.visual_style: Practical marketing site focused on freshness and value
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and practical; message is that great produce does not have to look perfect

branding.brand_signature: The term freeform for cosmetically imperfect produce

brand_strength.rationale: A clear positioning phrase and the freeform coinage, but searches found no press about the brand, merch or community, and the name is not explained.

outcome_analysis: Farmtheory stayed active and in February 2024 reported 3,000 partner farmers and more than 1,500 kitchens served after a $1.45M seed from Merak Ventures, four years after its YC batch. Sources show no big venture rounds and no distress, so the story is a slow, capital light supply chain business rather than a breakout or a failure. Whether the imperfect produce wedge scales beyond a niche is not shown by the sources.
notes: Seed of $1.45M is stated by Inc42 and listed by Entrepreneur India and Indian Startup News in search results. A $150,000 YC investment in March 2020 appeared in one search summary of Entrackr but I could not open the article, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Aggregators give conflicting totals ($1.6M, $1.96M, $3.6M) and a 2022 seed of $4M that matches no press; treated as unverified. YourStory lists the legal name as Livingtheory Technologies Pvt. Ltd. Outcome search found no shutdown, layoffs or acquisition. Founder backgrounds and education not found. Competitor source for Ninjacart is a search snippet of the 2016 YourStory article because the page itself returned 403.
